findings.reason: Narrowed privacy to the default local comparison workflow; removed the universal zero-upload heading. Same-catalogue/configuration reproducibility names the canonical body, not arbitrary report wrappers.

Replaced the unshipped/coming-next contradiction with implemented draft native registration and review-packet spec/CLI status. External timestamp acquisition stays gated. Renamed the mixed-status eyebrow to Draft capabilities.

Native parity is limited to the recorded registration fixture suite. Minimal-core in-toto fixtures are Python checker evidence; implementation parity is unverified. Added the pinned evidence target conformance matrix as a visible source on all three pages. Dormant compatibility copy is corrected too.

Scoped both the pipeline heading and lexing paragraph to Go/Rust token profiles. Kept the two-channel rule within that scope instead of asserting it for plain text, images or audio. W-0450 is changed by explicit context narrowing even though its own sentence is retained.
Changed the general copied-region wording to matching-region wording and removed original/copy relationship inference. The separately bounded synthetic worked example remains unchanged.
Separated replay of the report computation using identical catalogues/configuration from checking span contents, which also requires original bytes.

changed_fields.before: It is designed to cover any kind of work: source code, writing, images and audio. One shared evidence format sits underneath, with a profile for each medium. Your content never leaves your machine; only fingerprints are compared.
changed_fields.after: It is designed to cover any kind of work: source code, writing, images and audio. One shared evidence format sits underneath, with a profile for each medium. The default local comparison workflow keeps content on your machine and compares fingerprints locally.

changed_fields.before: Three local steps, zero content uploads
changed_fields.after: Three steps in the default local workflow

changed_fields.before: **Fragment and whole-file counts:** directional fragment containment reported alongside whole-file Jaccard similarity so a small copied region stays visible inside a larger file.
changed_fields.after: **Fragment and whole-file counts:** directional fragment containment reported alongside whole-file Jaccard similarity so a small matching region stays visible inside a larger file.

changed_fields.before: Traceweave helps you show where your work appears, and how copies relate to the original, with evidence anyone can check. It records facts. It leaves the judgments to people.
changed_fields.after: Traceweave records profile-specific similarity in checkable reports; it does not establish an original, authorship, ownership or copying. It records facts. It leaves the judgments to people.

changed_fields.before: **Coming next:** signed, timestamped registration records, so you can show a version of your work existed by a given date. Licence-history packets follow.
changed_fields.after: **Also implemented, in draft:** offline-first signed registration in Rust and Go, plus review-packet spec and CLI support. Obtaining external timestamps remains separately gated.

changed_fields.before: Re-run a comparison from catalogues and pinned configuration bytes to verify every count and span in a received report independently.
changed_fields.after: Re-run the report computation from the same catalogues and pinned configuration bytes. Checking spans against the original content also requires those original bytes.

changed_fields.before: Traceweave puts one shared evidence format underneath profile-specific extractors. Every comparison runs in three local steps so your content stays on your machine and anyone with the same catalogues can reproduce the exact report bytes.
changed_fields.after: Traceweave puts one shared evidence format underneath profile-specific extractors. In the default local comparison workflow, content stays on your machine; anyone with the same catalogues and configuration can reproduce the canonical report body.
The Go and Rust token-profile pipeline

changed_fields.before: A profile lexer scans UTF-8 input bytes with pinned `Unicode {{fact:spec.unicodeVersion}}` tables — no parser, compiler, or network access. It produces two streams: an **exact** channel keeping names and literals, and a **normalized** channel clearing identifier and literal values so simple renaming still aligns.
changed_fields.after: For the Go and Rust token profiles, a lexer scans UTF-8 input bytes with pinned `Unicode {{fact:spec.unicodeVersion}}` tables — no parser, compiler, or network access. It produces two streams: an **exact** channel keeping names and literals, and a **normalized** channel clearing identifier and literal values so simple renaming still aligns.
